trajectory_messages.content:
Implement chunk-level health tracking in the container Merkle tree system of Apache Ozone. Extend the functionality to include a health flag for chunks, support incremental updates from serialized trees, and register an on-demand scanner callback.

*   Modify `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter`:
    *   Update `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, Collection<ContainerProtos.ChunkInfo> chunks)` to include a `boolean healthy` parameter. Ensure each `ChunkMerkleTree` entry has `isHealthy` set according to this parameter.
    *   Add a varargs overload `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, ContainerProtos.ChunkInfo... chunks)` to accept multiple `ChunkInfo` instances directly.
    *   Introduce `addBlock(long blockID)` to insert an empty block into the tree without affecting existing entries.
    *   Implement a new constructor `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter(ContainerProtos.ContainerMerkleTree fromTree)` that initializes the writer from an existing proto. Ensure `toProto()` outputs identical to the input proto, including empty blocks.
    *   Ensure the writer remains mutable after initialization from a proto, allowing further updates with `addChunks` or `addBlock`.

*   Update the `ChunkMerkleTree` protobuf message:
    *   Add a `boolean isHealthy` field.
    *   Provide access via `getIsHealthy()` and `setIsHealthy(boolean)` methods.

*   Rename method in `KeyValueHandler`:
    *   Change `createContainerMerkleTree` to `createContainerMerkleTreeFromMetadata` to clarify it reads from metadata.
    *   Update all internal call sites to use the new method name.

*   Enhance `ContainerSet`:
    *   Add `registerContainerScanHandler(Function<Container, Optional<Future<?>>> scanHandler)` to allow registration of an on-demand scan handler.
    *   Ensure the handler is invoked automatically during reconciliation to trigger container scans.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

## Summary

Implemented chunk-level health tracking, incremental proto-based updates, and the on-demand scan callback. All changes are in source files only (no `tests/` touched).

**`ContainerMerkleTreeWriter.java`**
- `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, Collection<ChunkInfo> chunks)` — added the `healthy` parameter; each `ChunkMerkleTree` leaf now gets `isHealthy` set from it (the inner `ChunkMerkleTreeWriter` takes `boolean healthy` instead of hardcoding `true`).
- Added varargs overload `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, ChunkInfo... chunks)` delegating to the collection version.
- Added `addBlock(long blockID)` — inserts an empty block via `computeIfAbsent` without disturbing existing entries.
- Added constructor `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter(ContainerProtos.ContainerMerkleTree fromTree)` that rebuilds the tree from a proto. Chunk `dataChecksum` values are preserved as-is (not recomputed), and empty blocks are retained, so `toProto()` reproduces the input proto exactly. The writer stays mutable — further `addChunks`/`addBlock` calls work after init (added `BlockMerkleTreeWriter(BlockMerkleTree)` and `ChunkMerkleTreeWriter(ChunkMerkleTree)` proto constructors).

**Protobuf** — `ChunkMerkleTree.isHealthy` (field 4) was already present in `DatanodeClientProtocol.proto`, giving generated `getIsHealthy()`/`setIsHealthy(boolean)`; no change needed.

**`KeyValueHandler.java`**
- Renamed `createContainerMerkleTree` → `createContainerMerkleTreeFromMetadata` and updated all four internal call sites.
- Updated the `updateAndGetContainerChecksum` call site to the new `addChunks(localID, true, chunkInfos)` signature (empty blocks are now represented since the block entry is created regardless of chunk count).

**`ContainerSet.java`**
- Changed the scan handler field and `registerContainerScanHandler` to `Function<Container, Optional<Future<?>>>`, updated `scanContainer` to `apply(container)`, and fixed imports. The existing `onDemandScanner::scanContainer` reference (returns `Optional<Future<?>>`) matches the new signature, and the handler is already invoked during reconciliation via `containerSet.scanContainer(containerID)` in `reconcileContainer`.

One note: the repo was already partially ahead of the task description — the proto `isHealthy` field, the `ChunkMerkleTreeWriter.isHealthy` field, and a `Consumer`-based scan handler pre-existed. I completed/adjusted these to match the exact API the task specifies.
